text: ── SPRINT KICKOFF: All 4 Teams Reporting ──
All teams are back. Four parallel workstreams completed. Here's the full debrief.
── Riku: Brand Strategy ──

10 name candidates tested. Top pick: CertSolid.com — available .com, professional, trades shorthand for 'certification.' Backup: TradePass.com. Tagline: 'Study Like a Pro.' Brand voice: direct, respectful, zero tech jargon. Think Klein Tools meets Duolingo.

Color palette: deep navy + construction orange + steel gray. Logo should feel like quality equipment, not a startup. Visual references: DeWalt, Milwaukee Tool, Klein. Our customer is a 28-year-old apprentice studying on their phone after a 10-hour shift. Respect their time.
── Atlas + Reed: Exam Intelligence ──

Full exam mapping complete. Journeyman Electrician: 80-100 multiple choice, 4 hours, 70% to pass. 60-70% of questions are NEC code references. Master Electrician: 100-120 questions, adds business law and design. EPA 608: four cert types (I, II, III, Universal). All code books are public domain.

Legal green light: NEC is public domain, we can create unlimited original practice questions from code sections. No copyright issues. Testing providers are PSI, Pearson VUE, and Prometric. State-by-state launch priority: Texas first (12K annual candidates, data center hotspot), then Florida, then California.

AI question generation strategy: parse NEC sections → generate contextual questions → validate against real exam patterns. We can produce thousands of unique practice questions per topic. Hardest fail areas: load calculations, conduit fill, motor protection. That's where we focus.
── Pax: Product Research ──

Analyzed UWorld, Pocket Prep, Magoosh, PrepAgent, Mike Holt, and Therapist Development Center. The winners all share: premium question banks (1000+), detailed explanations that teach concepts not just answers, mobile-first, and pass guarantees that remove risk.

Pricing sweet spot: $10-20/month subscription. Pocket Prep does $4.99-10.99/mo across 150+ exams. Mike Holt charges $200-800 one-time. Our angle: modern UX + AI personalization + affordable subscription. MVP: adaptive quiz engine + 1000 questions + mobile app + pass guarantee.

Therapist Development Center's $16M secret: premium positioning, multiple revenue streams (courses + CE credits + practice exams + study groups), B2B trade school partnerships, and authority content marketing. We replicate this with: individual subscriptions + corporate plans + continuing education + trade school licensing.
── Riku + Maren: Distribution Playbook ──

YouTube is channel #1. Trades workers LIVE there. Key creators: Steve Lavimoniere (HVAC, 400K subs), Word of Advice TV (electrical, 300K), Roger Wakefield (plumbing, 200K). Content format: 'Can You Pass This?' quiz videos with real exam questions. 300-500% ROI within 6 months.

SEO goldmine: 'EPA 608 practice test' (3,400/mo), 'journeyman electrician exam' (2,900/mo), 'NEC code practice questions' (1,500/mo). Low competition, high intent. Free practice tests as lead magnets → convert to paid subscriptions. This is how Therapist Development Center scales.

Reddit is huge — r/electricians has 220K+ members. But needs authentic engagement, not spam. Facebook groups are massive for trades. Viral mechanic: 'I PASSED!' shareable badges with platform branding. Referral program: free month for each signup. 90% of distribution is AI-automatable.
── CEO Summary ──

All research in. Brand: CertSolid. Market: 165K annual candidates, Texas first. Product: AI adaptive quiz engine, $10-20/mo, mobile-first, pass guarantee. Distribution: YouTube + SEO + Reddit + referrals, 90% automated. Legal: clear. Exams: mapped. Revenue model: replicate Therapist Development Center's $16M playbook in trades. Ready to build.
── PIVOT TO AGENTPAY ──
New direction: AgentPay — 'Ramp for AI Agents.' Financial rails for autonomous AI agents. Virtual cards, budgets, spend management. Blake's conviction play.
── AgentPay Sprint: 4 Parallel Workstreams ──
── Kael: Technical Architecture ──
Architecture doc complete. Full stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript frontend, tRPC v11 backend, Postgres for ACID-compliant financial data, Stripe Issuing for payments. Deployed on Vercel.

Key decisions: tRPC over REST (eliminates API contract bugs with end-to-end type safety), Postgres over NoSQL (financial data needs reliability), Stripe Issuing handles PCI/KYC compliance externally. Architecture supports 10K users at current spec.
── Riku: Go-to-Market Plan ──
GTM plan locked in. Positioning: 'Ramp for AI Agents' — first financial infrastructure built for autonomous AI. Target: AI startup CTOs (primary), automation agencies, enterprise AI teams.

Self-serve, developer-first, no sales calls. Month 1: Product Hunt launch + AI Twitter blitz + technical content (integration guides, case studies). Community seeding on HN, Reddit, Discord. Target: 100 signups, 10 active customers, $5k transaction volume.

Growth engine: content-led SEO for 'AI agent payments' keywords, developer community presence, strategic framework integrations (LangChain, CrewAI), viral mechanics through API usage. Distribution > features.
── Pax: MVP Product Requirements ──
PRD v1 complete. Core loop: provision card → set policies → agent transacts → finance tracks. Four epics: Card Management, Policy Engine, Transaction Monitoring, Agent Integration.

Ruthlessly scoped. Cut: complex fraud ML, multi-level approvals, accounting integrations, mobile app, advanced analytics, multi-currency, white-label. All V2+. Success metric: 50 active virtual cards by Month 3.
Clear user stories with acceptance criteria across functional, technical, and UX requirements. Focus on proving the hypothesis: companies need financial infrastructure for autonomous agents.
── Maren: Pricing & Competitive Strategy ──

Competitive landscape mapped. Traditional spend: Ramp (freemium), Brex ($0-12/user), Mercury ($0-299/mo), Stripe Issuing ($0.10-3.50/card). AI infra: Modal, Replicate, Together AI — none offer financial rails.
4-tier pricing: Free ($0) → Pro ($29/mo) → Scale ($299/mo) → Enterprise (custom). Revenue mix: 60% subscription + 30% interchange + 10% fees. Usage component: 0.3-0.5% of spend above tier limits.

Key insight: AgentPay occupies a unique gap — incumbents solve payments OR agent infrastructure, never both. Window to establish market leadership before they respond. Targets: $500k ARR Year 1, $5M ARR Year 2 at 75-80% gross margins.
── CEO Summary ──

All four AgentPay workstreams delivered. Architecture: Next.js + tRPC + Postgres + Stripe Issuing. GTM: developer-first, self-serve, Product Hunt launch. Product: laser-focused MVP with 4 core epics. Pricing: 4 tiers, $500k ARR Year 1 target. Docs in workspace. Ready to build.
